Thanks for the context. High-level legal view and proposed redlines below. I kept the language modular so we can mix and match "cap basis" + multiplier + carve-outs.

1) Core choices on "cap basis":
- Prior 12 months (rolling): ties liability to recent run-rate and is standard for SaaS with annualized spend. Pros: predictable exposure, easier to model. Cons: may underrepresent multi-year, pre-paid commitments.
- Aggregate term: multiplies total paid across the contract term. Pros: captures larger pre-paid commitments. Cons: larger upside exposure for Redwood; harder to cap for long terms.

2) Multiplier guidance:
- 1x fees (conservative for Redwood) – common for standard SaaS.
- 1.5x–2x fees (compromise) – acceptable for strategic, higher-value deals.
- Flat high cap (e.g., $5M) – rarely acceptable for us unless contract economics justify.

3) Reset mechanic:
- Annual/rolling 12-month reset: limits per-year exposure and addresses their GC concern. Good middle ground if multiplier >1.
- Aggregate (no reset): Redwood assumes full multi-year exposure; acceptable only with conservative multiplier and added limitations.

4) Carve-outs we should accept:
- Gross negligence, willful misconduct, and IP infringement should remain carve-outs (we typically accept these).
- Data breach / security incidents: accept carve-out for breach caused by gross negligence or willful misconduct; push back on full carve-out.
- Regulatory fines: we should not accept carve-out for statutory fines.

Proposed redline snippets (pick A or B):

Option A (Sales-friendly - Rolling 12 months, 1x):
"LIMITATION OF LIABILITY. EXCEPT FOR LIABILITY ARISING FROM: (A) GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT; (B) INFRINGEMENT OF THIRD-PARTY INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY; OR (C) OBLIGATIONS FOR PAYMENT TO REDWOOD, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT EXCEED THE GREATER OF (I) THE TOTAL AMOUNTS PAID OR PAYABLE BY CUSTOMER TO REDWOOD IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO LIABILITY, OR (II) ONE HUNDRED THOUSAND DOLLARS (US $100,000)."

Option B (Compromise - Annual reset, 1.5x for single-year fallback):
"LIMITATION OF LIABILITY. EXCEPT FOR LIABILITY ARISING FROM: (A) GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT; (B) INFRINGEMENT OF THIRD-PARTY INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY; OR (C) OBLIGATIONS FOR PAYMENT TO REDWOOD, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT EXCEED THE GREATER OF (I) ONE HUNDRED FIFTY PERCENT (150%) OF THE AMOUNTS PAID OR PAYABLE BY CUSTOMER TO REDWOOD DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO LIABILITY (ROLLING), OR (II) THREE (3) TIMES THE AMOUNTS PAID TO REDWOOD DURING ANY SINGLE CONTRACT YEAR DURING THE TERM, OR (III) ONE HUNDRED THOUSAND DOLLARS (US $100,000)."

Notes / trade-offs: Option A is the cleanest for sales velocity. Option B gives Helios a stronger safety net while preventing unlimited aggregate exposure for Redwood. If Helios insists on aggregate term cap, propose: 1.25x–1.5x aggregate term multiplier with additional limitations (cap on damages types and reduced carve-outs).

Laura: on pricing impact — quantify expected exposure bands under A/B/C for the next five years with discounting assumptions and we can present to Finance.

If Sales wants to close quickly, my recommendation: present Option B as a counter (annual reset, 150% rolling / 3x single-year fallback). It is defensible and marketable.

Anita — thanks for sending and for the clarity on GC's position. We've reviewed and propose the following balanced counter to their redlines (short form):

Proposal (Redwood counter):
- Cap basis: Rolling 12-month lookback (addresses Helios's desire to protect against annual volatility).
- Multiplier: 150% (1.5x) of amounts paid in the 12 months immediately preceding an event giving rise to liability.
- Single-year fallback: If Customer demonstrates a single contract year with materially higher payments, an alternative single-year cap of 3x that year's fees applies.
- Floor: Minimum cap of US $100,000 (for low-spend arrangements).
- Carve-outs: Accept exceptions for gross negligence, willful misconduct, and IP infringement. For security incidents, accept carve-out only where proven gross negligence or willful misconduct. Regulatory fines remain excluded.

Rationale: This gives Helios stronger annual protection than a straight 1x while preventing Redwood from assuming unlimited aggregate exposure over a multi-year pre-pay. It is Markus's recommended middle ground and should be acceptable to finance/legal on our end.

Next steps:
- Anita: can you confirm whether Helios can agree to a rolling 12-month basis with a 1.5x multiplier and the single-year 3x fallback? If yes, we'll prepare a tracked-change MSA and updated order form.
- Laura and Markus: I'll put together the tracked redline and a 1-page impact note for the procurement packet and finance approval by EOD Wednesday.
